title: Large Language Models Are Biased Because They Are Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Theoretical analysis of the foundational assumptions of LLMs (e.g., the distributional hypothesis, cross-entropy optimization) to argue that societal biases are inherently baked into the models' latent structures and cannot be separated from linguistic meaning.

Theoretical linguistic analysis using the profession 'nurse' to illustrate how models fail to distinguish between non-contingent definitional facts (healthcare worker) and normatively unacceptable contingent statistical associations (gender pronouns or clothing).

Discussion and conceptual evaluation of existing empirical findings (e.g., African American dialect-based prejudice) to argue that alignment techniques like RLHF only superficially mask deeper covert racism.
